questions.question: The price of a sweater was slashed from ₹1422 to ₹1264 by a shopkeeper in the winter season. Find the rate of discount given by him ( Correct to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Total discount given = ₹1422 - ₹1264 = ₹158

Discount percentage = 158over1422 × 100 = 11.11%

**The discount percentage offered is 11.11%.**

questions.question: The average of nine numbers is 20.6. The average of three of them is 26.1, while the average of another three of these numbers is 15.2. What is the average of the remaining three numbers?
questions.solution:
**Formula:**

Average = Sum of the numbers/Total numbers

Calculation: 

Sum of 9 numbers = 20.6 × 9 = 185.4

Sum of 3 numbers of them = 26.1 × 3 = 78.3

Sum of another 3 numbers = 15.2 × 3 = 45.6

The Sum of remaining three numbers = 185.4 - (78.3 + 45.6) = 61.5

⇒ Average of remaining three numbers = 61.5/3 = 20.5

∴ The average of remaining three numbers is 20.5.

questions.question: The average marks of 100 students in a class were 80. The average marks of the top 15 students and the bottom 15 students in the merit list were 84 and 74, respectively. Find the average marks of the remaining students (correct to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average marks of 100 students were 80.

The average marks of the top 15 students is 84

and the average of the bottom 15 students is 74.

**Concept Used:**

No. of students × Average marks = Total obtained marks of the students

**Calculation:**

The total marks of 100 students = 100** **× 80

⇒ 8000 

The total marks of Top 15 students = 84 × 15

⇒ 1260

The total marks of Bottom 15 students = 74 × 15 

⇒ 1110 

So, total number of (15 + 15) = 30 students

⇒ Total marks of those 30 students = (1260 + 1110)

⇒ 2370

Total number of remaining students = (100 - 30)

⇒ 70 students

Total marks of remaining 70 students = Total marks of 100 students - Total marks of 30 students

⇒ (8000 - 2370)

⇒ 5630

So, the average marks of the remaining 70 students = 5630/70 = 80.43

**∴** **T****he average marks of the remaining students is** **80.43**

questions.question: A man borrows ₹13,000 to be paid back with the compound interest at a rate of 8% per annum compounded annually by the end of 2 years in two equal yearly instalments. How much will each instalment be?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

P = Rs. 13000 

R = 8%

T = 2 years

**Formula used: **

A = P (1 + R/100)T 

A = Amount, P = Principal

T = Time period, R = Rate of Interest

**Calculation: **

Let each instalment be x.

P for 1st installment, P₁ = x/(1 + 8/100)

⇒ P₁ = x/(108/100) = 100x/108

P for 2ⁿd installment, P2 = x/(1 + 8/100)²

⇒ P₂ = x/(1 + 8/100)² = 10000x/11664

Now,

P₁ + P₂ = 13000

(100x/108) + (10000x/11664) = 13000

20800x/11664 = 13000

x = 13000 × 11664/20800

x = 7290

**∴ The instalment each year is Rs. 7290. **

⇒ x/108 + 100x/108*108 = 130

⇒ x/108(1 + 100/108) = 130

⇒ 208x/108 = 14040

⇒ x = Rs. 7290

∴ The instalment each year is Rs. 7290.

questions.question: A man covered a distance of 245 km in 7 hours on a scooter. How much distance (in km) can be covered on a electric cycle in 4 hours, if he rides the electric cycle at 3/7 of the speed of the scooter?

Speed of the electric cycle = 3/7 × 35 = 15 km/h

⇒ Required distance = (15 × 4) = 60 km

**∴ 60 km can be covered by the electric cycle. **

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought two pairs of shoes at the same price and sold one pair at a profit of 15% and the other pair at a loss of 5%. if the difference between their selling prices is ₹140, then how much profit did he earn in the whole transaction?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the cost price (CP) of each pair of shoes be 100%.

The selling prices are 115% (15% profit) and 95% (5% loss).

Difference in selling price = 115% − 95% = 20%.

Given 20% = ₹140 ⇒ 10% = ₹70.

Overall net profit = (+15%) − 5% = +10%.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹70.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/93a2652b6d2f3295c124fa989385421e29efa06563b98ffa689528a1b3c0b3a7.png] 

**Given:**

⇒ The cost price of both pairs of shoes is exactly the same.

⇒ Profit earned on the first pair = 15%

⇒ Loss incurred on the second pair = 5%

⇒ Difference between their selling prices = ₹140

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the cost price (CP) of each pair be 100 units.

⇒ Selling price of the first pair (SP₁) = 100 + 15% of 100 = 115 units

⇒ Selling price of the second pair (SP₂) = 100 − 5% of 100 = 95 units

⇒ Difference in selling prices = 115 units − 95 units = 20 units

⇒ Since 20 units corresponds to ₹140:

⇒ 1 unit = 140 ÷ 20 = ₹7

⇒ Cost Price of each pair = 100 × 7 = ₹700

⇒ Total profit earned = Profit on first pair − Loss on second pair

⇒ Total net profit = 15 units − 5 units = 10 units

⇒ Overall net profit = 10 × 7 = ₹70

**∴ The correct answer is ₹70.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Same Cost Price Rule

When two items are bought at the same Cost Price, the overall profit or loss percentage is the simple average of their individual profit and loss percentages.

Same Selling Price Rule

When two items are sold at the exact same Selling Price, one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%, there is always an overall net loss given by the formula (x² ÷ 100)%.

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit and Loss are always inherently calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise in the problem. Profit = SP − CP, and Loss = CP − SP.

questions.question: Initially, Rekha works at such a rate that she can complete a piece of work in 24 h, but she works at that rate only for 8 h. After that, she works in such a way that she can complete the remaining work in 9 h. Rekha has to complete this work in one working period, then how many h will she take to complete that work?
questions.solution:
Given:

Rekha works at a rate such that she can finish the work in 24 h

Concept used:

Total work = Efficiency of the worker × time taken by him

Calculation:

Let the efficiency of Rekha be x units/h

Now,

Total work = 24 × x

⇒ 24x

In 8 hours she will complete 8 × x = 8x units

Remaining work = 24x - 8x = 16x

If Rekha completes the remaining work in 9 hours then her efficiency = 24x/9

⇒ 8x/3

So,

The remaining work is completed = 16x/(8x/3)

⇒ 6 hours

Total time = 8 + 6

⇒ 14 hours

∴ She will take 14 hours to finish this work.
